title: Topical Berberine in the Management of Premature Ejaculation and/or Erectile Dysfunction: Observational Signals, Regulatory Progress, and a Mechanistic Comparison with Emerging Pharmacotherapeutic Approaches
content: Introduction: Premature ejaculation and erectile dysfunction affect hundreds of millions of people globally. The search for effective and tolerable pharmacotherapeutic options that are also affordable and acceptable to patients remains an active area of clinical need. The author previously proposed the topical use of berberine to address these conditions through modulation of endothelial homeostasis. This update reports expanded observational signals, regulatory progress, and a comparative mechanistic analysis positioning topical berberine against the most notable emerging investigational compound in this space. Methods: Observational information was obtained from patients who legally purchased and used the SFDA-approved cosmetic berberine-based formulation Plazmid™ gel under routine clinical care, and who provided informed permission for anonymized reporting of their clinical experience. Patient-reported improvements in intravaginal ejaculatory latency time were the principal outcome recorded. No randomization or blinding was applied; the observational phase is designed to inform and support the forthcoming randomized controlled trial. The author holds intellectual-property and commercial interests in the product described, fully disclosed on the title page. Results: Most treated patients reported improvements in intravaginal ejaculatory latency time, as communicated to and documented by the treating clinician. Some patients reported improvement in erection. This pattern was observed across all observational settings. No adverse effects have been reported to date; however, adverse-event capture was not standardized. The absence of randomization, blinding, a control group, and pre-specified data capture prevents causal inference, and placebo effects cannot be excluded. Conclusions: To the author's knowledge, topical berberine is among the few natural-product-derived topical candidates for this indication with cosmetic regulatory progress and multi-site clinician-led observational signals across different clinical settings. It remains a plausible and potentially low-cost investigational approach for premature ejaculation and/or erectile dysfunction. The accumulating observational signal, cosmetic regulatory progress, and biologically plausible mechanism support progression to a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, for which international collaboration is actively sought.
